title: How Much Water Does AI Really Use?
hook: Nationally, AI data centers are 'a drop in the bucket' of total water use. Locally, a single one can drain a town's supply. Both things are true — which is what makes the debate tricky.
key_points: Across a whole country, AI data centers use a tiny share of total water — a drop in the bucket.
But one moderately sized center can have an outsized impact on its local water supply.
Amazon disclosed its data centers used about 2.5 billion gallons of water last year — reportedly a first.
The honest answer isn't 'huge' or 'nothing' — it depends heavily on scale and location.
content_html: The "AI is boiling the planet's water" headlines and the "it's totally fine" rebuttals can't both be right — so which is it? Ars Technica's answer is a useful both/and: when you add up all the water a country uses, AI data centers are, for now, a drop in the bucket. But that national average hides the local picture, where even a moderately sized data center can put real strain on the water supply of the specific town or region that hosts it.
extra_html: Both facts matter, and confusing them is where the debate goes wrong. Quote a national statistic and AI's thirst looks trivial; stand next to a single facility competing with a community for water during a drought and it looks alarming. The transparency around the numbers is also shifting: The Verge reported that Amazon — just after Seattle enacted a one-year data center moratorium that some of Amazon's own employees had pushed for — disclosed that its data centers used about 2.5 billion gallons of water last year, reportedly the first time it had shared the figure. The honest takeaway for a curious reader is to be skeptical of any one-line verdict. AI's water footprint isn't "nothing" and it isn't "the end of the world" — it's a real, uneven cost that depends enormously on where the computers sit and how they're cooled.

related.title: AI's Energy & Water
related.hook: Every chatbot reply runs in a warehouse of power-hungry computers somewhere. AI's convenience has a real physical footprint — in electricity, water for cooling, and carbon.

related.title: Communities Are Pushing Back on AI Data Centers
related.hook: The warehouses that power AI need land, power, and water — and neighbors are starting to say no. New York just signed the nation's first statewide data center ban into law.

flashcards.prompt: Which statement best captures AI data centers' water use?

choices.text: Small as a share of national use, but potentially huge for the local area
Enormous everywhere — it's draining the country's water
Zero — data centers don't use water

flashcards.explanation_html: Nationally it's a small fraction of total water use, yet a single facility can strain its local supply. Scale and location are what matter.

flashcards.prompt: What did Amazon reveal about its data centers' water use?
flashcards.back_html: Amazon disclosed that its data centers used roughly 2.5 billion gallons of water last year — reportedly the first time it shared the figure.
